Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Attaching a short hero/snippet pack and a one-pager that outlines the co-sell value props we discussed. We're trying to get the AWS Marketplace product page language locked down this month so the field has assets for the co-sell pitch.

Key asks:
- Quick review of hero lines (we have three options) and a one-line benefit statement for the top of the page.
- Any red flags on the usage/price footnote language (we prefer simple usage billing phrasing).
- Call to action recommendations — should we push Private Offer vs. AWS Purchase?

Would love a short window next week to align and then we can build the Marketplace listing draft.

Alicia — thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (product marketing) and Vanessa (aws partnerships) to get copy and co-sell ops input.

Initial thoughts:
- Hero option #2 feels closest to our positioning but needs a tighter benefits line (call out latency and cost controls).
- Price/footnote: keep it simple; avoid per-minute language. We can include a short footnote about reserved capacity for Dedicated customers.
- CTA: recommend Primary CTA = "Get started (Contact sales)" and Secondary CTA = "Request Private Offer". We should not push direct AWS Purchase as primary for enterprise deals.

Next steps:
1) Marissa: can you draft 2–3 revised hero lines and a one-liner benefit that calls out performance + predictable pricing?
2) Vanessa: can you confirm the Marketplace SKU/tiering recommendations and whether Private Offer links are set up for Acme?
3) Alicia: if you can share any field FAQs, we can map copy to common objections.

I can host a 30-min call Wed (07/15) 10am PT if that works — propose we lock copy + CTA then.

—Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Thanks for the tag, Jonas. I reviewed the attachments and sketched a set of edits — attached (revised_snippets.docx). High level suggestions below.

TL;DR recommendations:
- Hero (preferred): "Production-grade LLM inference: predictable latency, optimized cost."
- Benefit one-liner (subhead): "Serve large language models with predictable throughput, built-in cost controls, and enterprise-ready security."
- Three bullets for the product page: 1) High-throughput runtime with continuous batching and KV caching; 2) Dedicated & private deployment options for compliance and isolation; 3) Cost controls and intelligent batching reduces per-token spend.
- Pricing/footnote: Suggested language: "Pricing varies by deployment type — hosted per-token pricing; reserved monthly commitments available for Dedicated deployments. Contact sales for Private Offers and enterprise discounts." Avoid technical billing terms on the top-level page.
- CTAs: Primary = "Contact sales" + hover tooltip "Request a Private Offer for enterprise pricing." Secondary = "Read docs" (link to marketplace docs).

Copy notes for co-sell: include a short partner blurb: "Available via AWS Marketplace with Private Offers for enterprise procurement." This helps field sellers understand procurement options quickly.

Attached: revised_snippets.docx (contains 3 headline variations, page-level copy and suggested SEO snippets).

A couple of open items for Vanessa/partnerships team:
- Can you confirm whether Acme is already set up for Private Offers or if we need to request Private Offer enablement?
- Any constraints from AWS on claims like "predictable latency" — Vanessa, if you know policy owners who can confirm, please add.

If the Wed 07/15 10am PT slot works, I can run a quick walkthrough of the copy and we can lock the final text for listing submission.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior PMM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
